Root-cause fix: getRpcUrl now falls back to each chain's public RPC

ALCHEMY_ARC_RPC (the server-side, non-NEXT_PUBLIC env var) is absent
from process.env in production, confirmed directly via a live
diagnostic - only NEXT_PUBLIC_ALCHEMY_ARC_RPC exists. scanner.ts's
getRpcUrl()/rpc() had no fallback for a missing URL, so isContract and
its siblings silently failed closed to false/undefined for Arc
specifically. contracts.ts's getServerPublicClient (viem's http()
transport) already self-heals by falling back to the chain's own
default RPC when the URL is undefined, which is why /api/scan appeared
to work correctly this whole time - it was quietly using Arc's public
RPC (rpc.mainnet.arc.io), not Alchemy.

getRpcUrl now falls back the same way, using each chain's own default
RPC (mainnet/base from viem/chains, arc from lib/chains) when the
Alchemy-specific env var is missing. Also reverts the is-contract
serialization workaround from a wrong hypothesis now that the real
cause is fixed, and removes all debug fields from its response.

Still worth setting ALCHEMY_ARC_RPC as its own Production env var in
Vercel (separate from NEXT_PUBLIC_ALCHEMY_ARC_RPC) for genuine
Alchemy-backed reliability instead of relying on this fallback.

Serialize is-contract's chain checks to fix a false negative on Arc

Promise.all-ing eth/base/arc's eth_getCode calls deterministically
returned a false "not a contract" for Arc specifically when run on
Vercel's production network path, for an address independently
confirmed to have real, verified bytecode there. Not reproducible from
a local machine, and the identical call made alone (not concurrent)
already succeeded reliably elsewhere in the codebase (scanContract's
own isContract check). Serializing removes whatever contention causes
it, matching the same pattern already used for the Etherscan calls in
this file's sibling logic.

Route Arc through Etherscan V2, verify contracts, finish ownership migration

Etherscan added Arc mainnet to its unified V2 chainlist within a day of
launch (chain 5042, arc.etherscan.io) - confirmed live. scanner.ts now
routes Arc through the same ETHERSCAN_BASE path as ETH/Base instead of
the fail-closed placeholder from launch day, removing the special case
entirely. Both SalvageRecoveryRouter and SalvageBatchWrapper are now
source-verified on arc.etherscan.io and Sourcify, confirmed independently
via the Etherscan API returning real source for both. Explorer links
across the app now point to arc.etherscan.io instead of Circle's native
explorer, matching the Etherscan/Basescan naming pattern.

Also completes the router ownership migration on Arc: transferOwnership
from the deployer key, acceptOwnership from the SafePal hardware wallet,
matching ETH/Base. Verified via owner()/pendingOwner() reads before and
after each step.

Detect mis-sends to DEX pools/routers, add permissionless skim() recovery

Did I Lose Tokens? now flags transfers sent directly to known Uniswap V2
pools/routers, not just to a token's own contract. Pools are verified via
CREATE2 address recomputation against trusted factory bytecode (not name-
matching), so a permissionless skim() recovery button only ever appears
for cryptographically confirmed pools, scoped to the victim-flow claim
panel only.

Verified live on Base: a real direct WETH transfer to the WETH/USDC pool
is correctly detected end-to-end through /api/victim-scan, with
recipientKind/dexName/permissionlessRescue all populating from real
on-chain data.

Updates README and landing page FAQ to describe the new detection +
recovery path.

Fix hardcoded chain validation arrays blocking Arc requests

Four API routes (/api/scan, /api/victim-scan, /api/claims,
/api/blacklist-check) had their own literal ['eth', 'base'] checks
that never got touched by the earlier Chain-type sweep since they
don't match the Record<Chain,...> or union-type patterns that sweep
searched for. Missed until testing the actual live scan pipeline
against Arc caught it immediately - every Arc request was silently
rejected as "Invalid chain" regardless of everything else being
wired correctly.

Verified live against the real Arc Testnet Router and mock vault
through the actual /api/scan endpoint after the fix - full pipeline
now works end to end (Arcscan verification, rescue-function
detection, triage) exactly as it does for eth/base.

Wire Arc Testnet support across the app

Adds 'arc' as a third chain end to end: scanner.ts now routes ABI/
verification lookups to Arcscan since Arc isn't in Etherscan's V2
chainlist (confirmed directly), a custom viem chain definition since
Arc is too new for viem/chains, wallet config, chain selector UI, and
explorer/chain-name handling across every chain-aware surface in the
app (~16 files).

Backed by real verification, not just typechecks: contracts deployed
to Arc Testnet with production-matching config, verified on Arcscan,
and a full register -> send -> settle run against real Arc
infrastructure with every balance independently confirmed on-chain -
Arc's own docs warn local EVM simulators can't reproduce its actual
behavior, so this was tested live rather than trusted from Hardhat's
local network.

Uses testnet values (chain ID, contract addresses) as scaffolding,
clearly marked, pending Arc's mainnet launch on Sept 16.

Add AccessControl ownership detection for role-based contracts

The owner panel only recognized plain Ownable contracts before -
AccessControl has no single owner() to resolve, so nothing appeared
even for a wallet holding the relevant role. Now the scanner collects
every role-constant getter it can find in the ABI (DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE
first, falling back to any other _ROLE the contract declares), and a
new AccessControlOwnerGate checks each one live against the connected
wallet via hasRole() once it connects. A match renders the exact same
owner panel an Ownable contract gets - same trust model, same Send
button, no separate path.

Verified with unit tests covering real ABI edge cases, plus a live
check against a real 5-role OpenZeppelin TimelockController on
mainnet. Also updated the README for the Send button feature from
last session, which never got documented.

Add in-app rescue execution: a Send button on the owner panel

Fires the same decoded calldata the Copy Raw Calldata button already
produces directly via sendTransaction, so recovery no longer requires
leaving Salvage to paste it into Etherscan. Distinguishes a rejected
send from a broadcast-but-reverted one (checked via receipt status),
since a call into a contract Salvage doesn't audit can fail either way.

Verified two ways: a mock Hardhat test proving the mechanism (calldata
built the same way the frontend builds it correctly funds the claim
receiver and settles with the right split; a non-owner sending the
same calldata cannot pull the funds), and a live end-to-end run on
Base mainnet against a verified mock contract - Register, real Send,
Settle, independently confirmed on-chain.

Also fixed a latent flakiness in the routers expired-signature test
(compared wall-clock time instead of the chains own clock), and gave
MockERC20 real Transfer events on mint/transfer - without them, its
balances are invisible to Alchemy-style indexers that discover ERC-20
holdings via event logs rather than raw state, which is what blocked
the live verification until fixed.

Add 32x32 SVG icon for Etherscan token-update submission

Same brand mark as src/app/icon.svg, just declared at the exact
dimensions Etherscan's form requires instead of 52x52.

Stop tracking build-artifact files that churn on every dev/build run

tsconfig.tsbuildinfo (TS incremental cache) and next-env.d.ts (rewritten
differently by Next/Turbopack depending on dev vs build) add noise, not
real changes, to every commit that touches them.

Add ENS/Basename/Farcaster reverse-lookup for contact discovery

Resolves a scanned contract's owner/deployer, and any wallet searched
by someone other than its own connected owner, to a human identity —
turns the outreach template from a dead end into an actual contact
path. ENS + Farcaster confirmed working live; Basename implemented
per ENSIP-19 but reverts at the protocol level for every account
tested right now, documented honestly in the README.
Fix OG image dot color to match the canonical monochrome sonar mark

Update README for the Chrome Web Store launch

Extension is live now, not pending review - updates the feature
description, repo layout note, and moves it from In progress to
Shipped v1.4 in the roadmap.

Chip-style link in the warning bubble, center the popup on mobile

Underlined Check it on Salvage link is now a chip matching the rest
of the app's link style. Also centers the toolbar popup on hosts that
render it as a full-height panel (e.g. Kiwi Browser) instead of pinning
it to the top-left. Bumps to v1.0.1 for the Chrome Web Store update.

Block settlement into blacklisted recipients, plus small doc fixes

settle() reverts entirely if any one payout leg is blacklisted by the
token issuer, permanently stranding funds - checks victim/finder/protocol
before offering Settle and hides it if blocked. Also documents this in the
README, adds a FAQ entry, and fixes the stale $220K/10-10-tests figures.

Fix finder registration rejecting smart-wallet signatures

Same bug as the mini-app: plain viem verifyMessage() only supports EOAs.
Any finder connected via a smart contract wallet got a false Invalid
signature on every registration attempt.
Chip-style links on Privacy and Terms pages

Add Terms of Service, rate-limit the receipt route, update roadmap

/api/receipt/[type] was the one image route with no rate limiting - exactly
what gets hammered by social-preview crawlers once receipts are shared
publicly. Terms of Service covers no guarantee of recovery, the fixed
non-negotiable fee schedule, finder priority, and that Salvage never
custodies funds or controls outcomes - linked from every footer. Roadmap
gains Mini App batch settlement, AccessControl detection, and
multisig/timelock-aware triage: a Gnosis Safe as owner now reads as
needing signer coordination instead of a flat verdict.

Require a victim address on GET /api/claims

Without it the endpoint returned the 50 most recent claims across all
victims, unfiltered — nothing in the app calls it that way, so this
closes an easy full-registry-scrape path at no cost to real usage.

Replace tx/contract reference links and Share triggers with chips

Adds .chip-link (+ settled/on-dark variants) and .chip-btn, applied
across claim/find cards, /recoveries, /find, and the landing footer's
Router links, so all these small action/reference elements share one
consistent pill style instead of plain colored text.

Replace the GitHub-redirect Docs link with a real in-app docs page

Adds /docs covering the recovery flow, fee schedule, every feature,
security model, deployed contracts, and FAQ. Links (TOC, contract
addresses, support) use a consistent chip style instead of raw
underlined text.

Add a recoveries history page with per-item share receipts

salvage_claims lacked a recipient_contract column, so past recoveries
couldn't show their contract. Added it, populate going forward, and
degrade gracefully for old rows. New /recoveries mirrors /finds.

Replace share-page navigation with an in-place popover

window.open() after an awaited navigator.share() gets silently
blocked by desktop popup blockers. New popover avoids navigation
entirely: shows the card, copies the image to clipboard, and offers
one-click Share on X / Farcaster.

Add a visual receipt preview page, fix desktop share responsiveness

Share pointed at the raw image URL directly -- unpredictable on some
desktop share targets, no visible feedback either. New /receipt/[type]
page shows the card, sets it as the OG image, links to the homepage.
Falls back to opening this page when navigator.share is unavailable.

Show the find-registered Share button for pending finds too

The button only checked claimStatus === registered_for_you (the
on-chain claim state), missing pending -- which is where a find sits
until an on-chain claim is separately registered. Every row on /finds
already represents a registered find, so both states should show it.

Surface newly-settled finds to finders on their next visit

Finders are rarely online when their find settles. Welcome-back panel
now tracks seen findKeys per wallet and highlights new settlements.

Add shareable receipt cards for find registration and settlement

New /api/receipt/[type] route renders a shareable image via next/og --
find registration and settlement (victim/finder framing differ). Wired
into FinderFindCard, RecoveryClaimPanel, and OwnerClaimPanel.

Deepen the finder earnings panel: full timeline, earned $, lifetime totals

Only one tx link showed before (dropping the other), no earned $, no
lifetime totals. All three now shown, computed from data already in memory.

Number Recent Activity rows and paginate the finds page

Matches Leaderboard's existing numbering (kept the type emoji too).
Finds page had no pagination at all -- now capped at 5 per page.

Pad gas estimates for batch register/settle transactions

batchRegisterClaims/batchSettle had no explicit gas parameter, relying
entirely on the wallet's default estimate/buffer. Per-item cost varies
widely (skipped item vs. full CREATE2 deploy + transfers), so a batch
where every item hits the expensive path can starve whichever item
runs last -- observed live on Base, where the 5th of 5 claims in a
settle batch reverted with out-of-gas while the first 4 succeeded.
Now estimates gas explicitly and pads it +30%, falling back to the
wallet default if estimation itself fails.

Add the SalvageRecoveryRouter ownership-transfer script

One-off script used to migrate the router owner role from the deployer
key to a SafePal hardware wallet on both chains, completed 2026-07-19.
Kept as a historical record of how the transfer was done, same as
deployRouter.ts documents the original deployment.

Disclose the Chrome extension's behavior in the privacy policy

The policy never mentioned that content.js watches every text field on
every page for address patterns before sending a match to our own API.
Needed before Chrome Web Store review, which scrutinizes the
<all_urls> + host_permissions combination closely.

Document the unpacked-load path issue in the extension README

Loading unpacked straight from this repo path caused Chrome to
intermittently fail fetching the service worker script (status code 3),
with popup delays from seconds to minutes before being flagged crashed.
Traced to something blocking Chrome file access to that specific path,
not the code -- a copy at an unrelated path loaded instantly and stayed
fast. Doesn't affect published/Web-Store users, only local unpacked dev.

Bound the whole checkAddress operation, not just the fetch

A hung chrome.storage.session call wasn't covered by the fetch timeout,
so it could still hold the message channel open indefinitely and get
the service worker flagged unresponsive. Race the whole operation
against a 9s ceiling instead. Also evict stale cache entries on read
so chrome.storage.session doesn't grow unbounded over a long session.

Bound the is-contract fetch with an 8s timeout

The fetch to usesalvage.xyz had no timeout, so a hung request could
hold the message channel open indefinitely -- symptom matched: the
popup/content-script warning would sit unresponsive, and the service
worker was reported as crashed shortly after.

Add rate limiting to finder-status, owner-status, and stats endpoints

These were the last three of eleven API routes without Upstash rate
limiting, left unthrottled while every other route already had it.
finder-status and owner-status run real per-wallet Supabase queries
(finder-status loops one per stranded token) with no cost/DoS guard.

Harden the background service worker against storage and messaging failures

Wrap the cache read in try/catch so a storage failure falls through to a
live check instead of hanging, and catch the sendResponse promise so an
unhandled rejection cant leave the popup stuck on Checking....

Don't flag EIP-7702 delegated EOAs as contracts in isContract()

eth_getCode returns non-empty bytecode for wallets that have an active
EIP-7702 delegation (Pectra), causing the extension and scanner to
misreport ordinary user wallets as contracts. Detect the reserved
0xef0100 delegation designator and treat it as an EOA.
